newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 9.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* German Chancellor Helmut Kohl maintains that his country will be ready to qualify for Europe's new single currency on time without softening the entry rules.
* Investors in mutual funds that specialize in technology stocks withdrew $62.5 million in the past week.
* The Clinton administration has faced one roadblock after another in its effort to open markets around the world.

* The Broadway landlord, Jujamcyn, and Pace Theatrical Group, which presents national touring shows, have an agreement to create a production and distribution system that would give birth to an idea, then chaperone it through Broadway and onto international tours.

* Big Brother is here, with electronic devices tracking people's movements virtually everywhere -- from making a withdrawal at an ATM machine to using a credit card to purchase an airline ticket -- making it easier for police to track down suspects.
* On-line businesses are seeking greater control over who hooks up to their sites, how they link and how their content is displayed.
* The United Auto Workers union has handed General Motors Corp two more strike deadlines on Friday, setting to stage for job actions at three auto parts factories.

* The publisher, Carroll & Graf, is churning out 50,000 books that contain former first lady Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis' last will and testament, charging $18 for something that could cost readers $10 to buy through probate court.
* A new breed of magazines has arrived on the scene that focuses on how to cope with a particular malady.
* The television networks are promoting their new fall lineups over the Internet.

* The fortunes of Voxware Inc, a Internet start-up, mirror the rest of the second-tier among technology stocks. Despite a market hot for technology stocks, Voxware's price is down 37 percent to $4.6875 from an offering price of $7.50 a share.

* The New Yorker magazine has named a cartoon editor for the first time since 1973, and the appointment comes at a time when it's increasingly difficult for young, unknown cartoonists to get their work published.
* BankAmerica Corp is expected to announce a $540 million cash deal to acquire Robertson, Stephens & Co, an investment firm.
